title: Affine coordinates of intrinsic derived self-Tor, for supplied augmented lifts
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme]. In the standard derived category [def-pc-derived-category] with its fixed derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], let B=i_*O_Z, D=Q(B[0]), and Q_n=H^{-n}(D tensor-derived D), for n≥0. For every affine open U let A_U=Gamma(Y,U), I_U=ker(i)(U), P_U the chosen projective resolution of A_U/I_U, and T_U=P_U tensor A_U/I_U [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. There exist A_U-linear equivalences c_U:H_n(T_U)≃Gamma(U,Q_n). For every basic inclusion V⊆U with ring restriction phi, and every supplied quotient homomorphism psi, augmented chain map a:P_U→Res_phi(P_V), and tensor chain map k:T_U→Res_phi(T_V), assume psi(mk(x))=mk(phi(x)), pi_V(a_0(x))=psi(pi_U(x)), and k_j(x tensor y)=a_j(x) tensor psi(y). Then restriction of c_U(x) equals c_V(e(H_n(k)(x))) for every x, where e is the exact restriction-of-scalars homology comparison. There is no supplied sheaf resolution, no boundedness hypothesis and no assertion that lifts exist.

source.place: Tag 08DX(2), affine derived tensor calculation; Tags 06YH, 01I9 and 00LS(2), for the normalized resolution and restriction comparisons

proof.text: On an affine U construct the coefficient identification by the quotient section map Gamma(Y,U)/ker(i)(U) to Gamma(i inverse U,O_Z), using surjectivity for a closed immersion with affine target (Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.isAffine_surjective_of_isAffine) and kerLift. Apply the tilde adjunction, normalized by that map; the affine quotient sheaf identification proves it is invertible. Extend the projective quotient resolution by embeddingDownNat. Its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, and its terms are flat by Module.Flat.of_projective, so bounded-flat K-flatness applies. Restrict intrinsic derived tensor to U and apply the affine derived tensor chart comparison to this specific resolution. This identifies it with the tilde of the algebraic total tensor.

Apply exact tilde homology comparison. Tensoring with the single quotient complex and extending the nonnegative tensor complex agree: in degree -j there is only the ( -j,0 ) summand, with differential d tensor id; positive degrees are zero. The extension homology isomorphism at -n identifies the homology with H_n(P tensor A/I). Compose with the normalized tilde section unit and with exact open restriction homology to obtain c_U. Each component is an isomorphism, so c_U is a linear equivalence. All equivalences use the same quotient section normalization.

For a basic inclusion and supplied psi,a,k, associate a to a map of the two sheafified resolutions using tilde adjunction. The augmentation formula makes its image under derived localization the coefficient restriction map: invert the augmentations and cancel them in the commuting square. The formula on pure tensors identifies the associated map of k with the tensor comparison map. Naturality of the derived tensor counit, the canonical affine tensor comparison, exact homology and the tilde section unit gives the displayed element equation after the restriction-of-scalars homology isomorphism. If different augmented lifts are used, the proved quotient tensor lift homotopy and Homotopy.homologyMap_eq give the same homology map. No lifting existence is asserted or needed in this lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_derived_selfTor_affine_coordinates
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := CochainComplex.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let D := DerivedCategory.Q.obj (S.obj B)
    let Q := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (-(n : ℤ))).obj (D ⊗ D)
    ∃ c : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens,
        ((((tensorRight (ModuleCat.of (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
          ((Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u) ⧸ i.ker.ideal U))).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)).obj
            (projectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
              ((Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u) ⧸ i.ker.ideal U))).complex).homology n) ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, U.1)]
              Q.val.obj (op U.1),
      ∀ (V U : Y.affineOpens) (h : V.1 ≤ U.1)
        (_hbasic : ∃ f : Γ(Y, U.1), Y.basicOpen f = V.1),
          let A := (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
          let C := (Γ(Y, V.1) : Type u)
          let I := i.ker.ideal U
          let J := i.ker.ideal V
          let φ := (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
          let P := projectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))
          let R := projectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ J))
          let TA := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.down ℕ)
          let TC := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ J))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.down ℕ)
          ∀ (ψ : (A ⧸ I) →+* (C ⧸ J))
            (a : P.complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
              (.down ℕ)).obj R.complex)
            (k : TA.obj P.complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
              (.down ℕ)).obj (TC.obj R.complex))
            (hψ : ∀ x : A, ψ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk J (φ x))
            (ha : ∀ x : P.complex.X 0, R.π.f 0 (a.f 0 x) = ψ (P.π.f 0 x))
            (hk : ∀ (j : ℕ) (x : P.complex.X j) (y : A ⧸ I),
              k.f j (x ⊗ₜ[A] y) = (show R.complex.X j from a.f j x) ⊗ₜ[C] (ψ y)),
            let e := ((TC.obj R.complex).sc n).mapHomologyIso
              (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ)
          ∀ x, Q.val.map (homOfLE h).op (c U x) =
            c V (e.hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap k n x))
